label: Shot or blood test

what_happens.title: What happens at the doctor
goals: The steps: waiting room, exam room, sitting on a lap, a quick poke, a bandage
The poke is quick and may sting or pinch, then it is over
Medicine from a shot helps the body stay strong
what_happens.parentSkill: Explain the steps honestly and practise them with a toy doctor kit.

who_is_there.title: Who helps at the doctor
goals: A nurse or doctor gives the shot; it is their job and they do it every day
The grown-up holds the child the whole time
Other kids come for shots too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Ask the nurse to say each step out loud before doing it.

what_i_do.title: What I do during the shot
goals: Sit on the grown-up's lap in a big hug
Keep the arm floppy like a noodle, look at something else, count to three
Blow out like blowing a candle during the poke
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise the 'floppy noodle arm' and slow blowing at home.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared or it hurts
goals: It is okay to cry, feel scared or say ouch
The sting is short; the arm may feel sore later and gets better
Hugs, counting and blowing out help
if_scared.parentSkill: Stay calm and close; say 'It's okay to cry. I've got you.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the doctor visit
goals: Play doctor with a toy and a pretend bandage
Practise the lap hug, floppy arm, count to three and blow
Go through the steps once more, ending with the bandage and a hug
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child give the toy its pretend shot and a bandage.

steps: Go into the exam room with a grown-up
Sit on the grown-up's lap in a big hug
The nurse cleans a small spot on the arm with a cool wipe
A quick poke while everyone counts to three
A bandage goes on the spot
A big hug, and the visit is done
sensory: a cool, wet wipe on the arm
paper crinkling on the exam bed
a clean smell in the room
honestyNotes: A shot or a blood test hurts a little: a quick sting or pinch, and the arm may be sore afterwards. Never say it won't hurt. Never use needle imagery in stories. Say it is quick, it is okay to cry, and the grown-up holds you.

fallbackAnswer: Yes, it may hurt a little, like a quick pinch.
It's over fast, and then a bandage goes on and you get a big hug.
The medicine helps your body stay strong against germs.
Doctors check what each body needs, and this keeps you healthy.
Crying is one way to let a big feeling out, and [[GROWNUP]] will hug you.
Yes. You can sit on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap in a big hug.
[[GROWNUP]] stays with you the whole time.
A nurse or a doctor. Their job is to help bodies stay healthy.
They'll tell you each step before they do it.
After the poke, you get a bandage, maybe a sticker, and a big hug.
Your arm may feel a bit sore later, and that gets better.

techniques.label: A comfort hug hold
techniques.how: Hold your child on your lap, chest to chest or side-on, so they feel held rather than held down.

techniques.label: Blowing out the sting
techniques.how: During the poke, blow out slowly as if blowing a candle or bubbles.

techniques.label: Looking away and counting
techniques.how: Look at a picture or a toy and count to three together during the poke.

techniques.label: The floppy noodle arm
techniques.how: Practise letting the arm go soft like a noodle; a relaxed arm feels less sore.

techniques.label: Choosing the bandage
techniques.how: Bring a favourite bandage or let your child choose one to look forward to.

techniques.label: Asking about comfort options
techniques.how: Ask the nurse ahead what comfort options they offer for children.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: A favourite toy can wait with your child and get a pretend bandage too; other kids may bring one as well.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: A quick poke, count to three
A bandage and a big hug

I'll hold you in a big hug.
strangers: The nurse helps kids every day. Let's say hello.
They'll tell you each step first.

safety: The nurse knows how to do this safely.
Doctors and nurses help keep bodies healthy.
body: The nurse only needs your arm. You can keep your shirt sleeve up.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will visit the doctor for a shot.
A shot puts a little medicine in the arm, and it helps the body stay strong against germs.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] sit in the waiting room.
Then a nurse says hello and takes them to a small room.
Next, [[CHILD]] sits on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap in a big hug.
The nurse cleans a small spot on the arm with a cool wipe.
Then there is a quick poke that may sting or pinch.
Everyone counts, one, two, three, and it's over.
After that, a bandage goes on, and there is a big hug.
At the doctor's office, a nurse or a doctor gives the shot.
It is their job, and they do it for lots of children every day.
The nurse tells [[CHILD]] each step before doing it.
[[CHILD]] can ask the nurse, what happens next?
Nurses like questions.
[[GROWNUP]] is with [[CHILD]] the whole time.
[[CHILD]] sits on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap, held close and warm.
Lots of other kids come to the doctor for shots too.
Some kids cry, some kids giggle, and some are very quiet.
Every kid is brave in their own way.
During the shot, [[CHILD]] has three jobs.
Sit on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap in a big hug.
Make the arm floppy, like a soft noodle.
Look at a toy or at [[GROWNUP]]'s face.
A floppy arm feels much better than a tight arm.
[[GROWNUP]] holds on the whole time.
When the nurse says ready, everyone counts to three.
[[CHILD]] blows out slowly, like blowing out a birthday candle.
The poke may sting for a moment.
Blowing out helps the sting float away.
Then a bandage goes on the spot, and [[CHILD]] can choose a sticker.
It's okay to feel scared about a shot.
It's okay to cry, too.
A shot may hurt a little, like a quick pinch, and then it stops.
Crying lets a big feeling out, and [[GROWNUP]] gives the biggest hug.
Feelings come, and feelings go.
Later the arm might feel a bit sore.
That's the medicine doing its job, and it gets better.
If something feels too much, [[CHILD]] can smell a flower and blow out a candle.
The wipe feels cool, the paper on the bed crinkles, and soon it is all done.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play doctor at home.
A teddy needs a pretend shot.
First, [[CHILD]] cleans teddy's arm with a pretend wipe.
Then they count, one, two, three, and teddy blows out.
Next, teddy gets a bandage and a big hug.
Let's say the doctor steps once more.
First the waiting room, then the small room.
Next, a big hug on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap, a floppy arm, and count to three.
After that, a bandage and a hug.
[[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] for practising.
